name: Hash functions

subjectOf.text: Hash functions let a leaderless network reach consensus on identity and ordering, because every node independently hashes a transaction's data and deterministically arrives at the same unique identifier that everyone recognizes.
subjectOf.abstract: Thanks to the hash function, every node in the network hashes the transaction's data and independently arrives at the same an- swer, giving the transaction a unique ID that everyone recognizes.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Contemporary Decentralization (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3782198
scope_conditions: requires all nodes to run the same deterministic hash protocol

subjectOf.text: A blockchain is immutable because any attempt to edit an old block changes the hash of that information and is immediately rejected by the network that follows the protocol.
subjectOf.abstract: The blockchain is immutable, because any attempt to edit the old blocks will be immediately rejected by the network. A single number or letter changed anywhere in its entire history will result in a different hash of the information.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Contemporary Decentralization (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3782198
scope_conditions: holds as long as the network keeps following the blockchain protocol
